persona.who: 21, Indian-American senior at Rutgers, born in NJ. Parents from Gujarat. Dating a white classmate; hasn't told parents. Feels neither fully Indian nor American.
persona.note: my parents keep asking when I'll 'settle down with a nice Gujarati boy' and I've been with my boyfriend for 2 years and he's not Indian. I feel like whichever way I go I lose a part of me

understanding.emotion: caught between two parts of herself
understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call being seen as less than you are, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: Seven days from being pressed to shrink to standing in the life you are already living, with the words to say so.

week_beats.hook: You recognise being asked to choose between two versions of yourself, and the anger of being told you lose either way.

understanding.core_struggle: A young woman under twenty-five is being pressed by her parents to marry a Gujarati boy while she is in a two-year relationship with a non-Indian man she does not want to leave.
understanding.mirror: You give them the answer they want, and you lose a piece of yourself.
understanding.insight: You are not choosing between them and your parents. You are choosing between two versions of yourself, and your parents' picture is not your size.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

queries.hook: Being asked to choose between a life they have drawn and the one you are already living, and the anger of being told you are losing yourself either way. My parents' expectations weigh on me.
queries.diagnose: When others see only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the harm deepens only when their picture begins to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what they see; your worth was never theirs to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture they hold.
queries.story: A young woman of learning and standing, dismissed by her own family for the life she chose, who questioned them openly and stood in her truth until they had no answer.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
verse.line: Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, even done imperfectly, than the duty of another well done. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is full of fear.
verse.why: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.
verse.misuse: Not 'stay in the role your family or birth assigned you'. It's about being true to your own nature and calling.

prasang.title: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasang.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna that it is better to do your own work, even if it is flawed, than to do someone else's work perfectly. Borrowed lives carry fear. This is not about staying in a role your family assigned you. It is about acting from your own nature, free of ego and the need to please. The verse asks you to trust the life you are already living.
verse.for_you: You are caught between your parents' picture of your future and the life you are actually living. You do not have to choose between them and your parents. Trust the path that is already yours.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Right after naming the five causes of any action, Krishna warns about the person who ignores four of them.
verse.sanskrit: तत्रैवं सति कर्तारमात्मानं केवलं तु यः । पश्यत्यकृतबुद्धित्वान्न स पश्यति दुर्मतिः ॥
verse.line: If you think you alone made it happen, or alone made it fail, you're not seeing the whole picture.
verse.translation: That being so, whoever, through an untrained understanding, sees himself alone as the doer does not truly see.
verse.why: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.
verse.misuse: Not a way to dodge responsibility; you are still one of the five causes.

prasang.title: What makes an action happen
prasang.summary: Every action has five causes: the setting, the doer, the instruments, the efforts, and providence. Seeing oneself as the only doer is a mistake.
prasang.lesson: You are one cause among five; own your part, not the whole outcome.

verse.meaning: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna after explaining that five forces shape every action: the setting, the doer, the tools, the effort, and providence. Krishna warns that if a person looks at an outcome and believes they alone made it happen, or that they alone caused it to fail, they are missing the full picture. The verse asks us to see ourselves as one cause among five, owning our part without claiming the entire result.
verse.for_you: You are not the only reason your parents are pushing this marriage. Their fear and their image of you are causes too. Own your part in choosing your life, but do not carry the whole weight of their disappointment.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula speaks to her son Sanjaya, who has lost his kingdom and lies defeated. She tells him not to hold himself in contempt, to stop settling for little, and to set his mind on what is truly good. She urges him to stop fearing and to pull himself together, because those who never try never succeed.
verse.for_you: Your parents' picture of you is small, and that hurts. But you are not a failure for wanting more. Set your mind on the life you are already building and stop letting their fear shrink your sense of what is good for you.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verse.sanskrit: त्वया व्याप्तमिदं विश्वं त्वयि प्रोतं यथार्थतः । शुद्धबुद्धस्वरूपस्त्वं मा गमः क्षुद्रचित्तताम् ॥
verse.line: You are pure awareness, wider than any worry. Don't let your mind shrink into pettiness.
verse.translation: This whole universe is pervaded by you and strung on you. By nature you are pure awareness; do not fall into smallness of mind.
verse.why: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

prasang.title: Janaka asks the boy-sage how to be free
prasang.summary: King Janaka, ruler of Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra three questions: how to gain wisdom, freedom and dispassion. Ashtavakra answers at once: you are not the body or your roles but the awareness that watches them, and freedom is available now.
prasang.story_hook: A powerful king bowed before a boy whose body was bent in eight places, and asked him how to be free.
prasang.lesson: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

verse.meaning: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how to become free. Ashtavakra answers that this whole universe is strung on you and by nature you are pure awareness. Do not fall into smallness of mind. You are the awareness that watches your roles and worries, not the roles or the worries themselves. Freedom is available the moment you stop shrinking.
verse.for_you: When your parents press you to marry someone you do not want, they are asking you to shrink. You are not the daughter they picture. You are the awareness that holds both their hopes and your own life. Let your mind stay wider than their picture of you today.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verse.sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Speak words that don't wound, that are true, kind and helpful. That is discipline of speech.
verse.translation: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
verse.why: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.
verse.misuse: Kind speech doesn't mean avoiding hard truths; it means saying them without cruelty.

prasang.title: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that the discipline of speech is to speak words that do not wound, that are true, kind and helpful. It is about giving without strings and dropping the show. Speech should be a gift, not a weapon, and it should be grounded in what is real.
verse.for_you: when the pressure to marry comes up, speak your truth without wounding. You do not have to fight to be seen as less than you are. Say what you feel, calmly and clearly, and let the words be a gift to yourself.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.setting: Ribhu on how a free person moves through the world.
verse.sanskrit: प्राप्तकर्मकरो नित्यं शत्रुमित्रसमानदृक् । ईहितानीहितैर्मुक्तो न शोचति न काङ्क्षति ॥ सर्वस्याभिमतं वक्ता चोदितः पेशलोक्तिमान् । आशयज्ञश्च भूतानां संसारे नावसीदति ॥
verse.line: Do the work in front of you, speak gently, read people's hearts, and you won't sink in the world.
verse.translation: Always doing the work that comes, seeing friend and foe alike, free of wanting and not-wanting, such a one neither grieves nor craves. Saying what is agreeable to all, speaking gently when asked, knowing the intent of others' hearts, such a one does not sink in the world.
verse.why: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

prasang.title: How a free person lives
prasang.summary: Ribhu describes how a free person lives among others: letting go of what is lost, taking up what comes, doing the work at hand, speaking gently, busy outside and calm inside, and treating the whole world as family.
prasang.lesson: Live fully in the world while staying unhurried inside.

verse.meaning: Ribhu speaks to Nidagha about how a person who is truly free lives among others. The free person does not cling to what is lost or crave what is not there. They do the work in front of them, treating friend and stranger with the same calm, and they speak gently and with truth. By knowing the intent behind people's words and speaking what is kind and useful, they do not drown in the world's demands. The teaching is to move through life fully and with purpose, while keeping an unhurried center inside.
verse.for_you: You are studying for exams and living your life. Let the work in front of you be your anchor. When your parents press you, speak gently but firmly about what you need. Do not let their noise drown out the life you are actually living.

story.title: Parvati holds to her choice
story.story_hook: The sages came to talk Parvati out of it, and they listed every flaw in the man she had chosen.
story.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.
story.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

anchor.speaker: Parvati
anchor.setting: Parvati answers the sages who mock her resolve to win Shiva through years of austerity.
anchor.sanskrit: सत्य कहेहु गिरिभव तनु एहा। हठ न छूट छूटै बरु देहा॥ कनकउ पुनि पषान तें होई। जारेहुँ सहजु न परिहर सोई ॥
anchor.line: Gold comes from stone, and even in fire it stays gold. Hold to what you are.
anchor.translation: You speak truly: this body was born of a mountain, so its resolve will not break, even if the body does. Gold too is born of stone, and even in fire it does not give up its nature.
anchor.why: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.
anchor.misuse: Steadiness is not stubbornness; keep checking that the goal is still worth it.

prasang.title: Parvati holds to her choice
prasang.summary: Reborn as Parvati, Sati resolves to marry Shiva and spends years in austerity. The seven sages come to test her, mocking Shiva as a homeless ascetic and offering her a better match. She answers that gold keeps its nature even in fire, and that the heart wants the one it has chosen.
prasang.story_hook: The sages came to talk Parvati out of it, and they listed every flaw in the man she had chosen.
prasang.lesson: Persistence is choosing the same thing again each day, even when others call it foolish.

story.for_you: Your parents want you to become someone you are not, like a stone shaped into gold. But you already know your shape. Hold to it, day after day, even when they call it foolish.

script: You are caught between two versions of yourself, and your parents' picture is not your size. You have been with your boyfriend for two years. You are fighting with your parents. They are pressing you to marry a Gujarati boy. You do not want to leave your boyfriend. You feel like they see you as less than you are.

Krishna is speaking to Arjuna on a battlefield. Arjuna is confused about what to do. He looks at the two armies and feels lost. Krishna tells him to act from his own nature instead of copying others. And Krishna replied:
श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात्, स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः.
In plain words: Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.

Krishna is saying that your own path, even if it is flawed, beats a borrowed one. A borrowed life is full of fear. It is easier said than done, because your parents want a perfect life for you. But the truth is, your nature is already here. You are already living it. You do not need to shrink to fit their picture.
Trust the life you are already living. You are not choosing between your boyfriend and your parents. You are choosing between their picture and your own truth. Let your own path be enough today.
What if your own path is already the right one?

depth.life: You are caught between two parts of yourself. Your parents want you to marry a Gujarati boy, but you have been with a non-Indian boyfriend for two years. They keep fighting with you, and their expectations feel heavy. You are not choosing between them and your parents. You are choosing between two versions of yourself.
depth.points: Borrowed lives are dangerous. Your parents' picture of your future is not your size. Their path is full of fear because it is not yours. Your own path, even if it feels imperfect or uncertain, is the only one that fits.
depth.practice: Take a moment to name one small thing that feels truly yours, like a song or a thought, and let it be enough for now.
depth.question: What is one small part of your life that already feels like your own?
